GFL lowered reference-relative CIEDE2000 in 24/26 objects, while visible pink or purple shifts remained in two legacy Fig.~4 cases under No Adapter, GFL, and LLH. Their mapping to the original submitted panels cannot be recovered; the traceable Fresh C example in Figure~\ref{fig:color-failure} is a different object and is not presented as a reproduction of those cases. The decoded RGB output showed the shifts before UV projection or baking, and a late denoising snapshot (update 40 of 50) showed one of them. In that case, a ground-truth VAE encode--decode isolate had CIEDE2000 4.086 and $\Delta a^*\approx-1.35$, compared with 22.032 and $+1.977$ for GFL. This weakens ordinary VAE round-trip error as the sole explanation in that case; it does not identify the complete cause or rule out other model and conditioning effects.

A locked P0 trace reproduced the archived RGB pixels for three preselected objects in repeated Python 3.13.5 runs; the Python 3.10 trace reproduced its corresponding archived observer. The first cross-runtime numerical divergence occurred after multiplying the identical FP16 initial latent by the scheduler's initial noise scale (maximum absolute difference 0.0625; RMSE 0.00966). This localizes an execution-stack difference, not the color-generation cause; the three-object trace does not establish cohort-wide cross-stack equivalence.

LLH--GFL also increased mean CIEDE2000 while reducing foreground gradient magnitude ($-0.06772$), high-frequency energy ($-0.00887$), and color entropy ($-0.598$). Lower local variation therefore did not imply better reference-color agreement or greater texture fidelity. The terminology follows Section~\ref{subsec:metrics}: texture variation, image-space agreement, reference-color agreement, subjective preference, baked 3D appearance, and PBR/material fidelity are reported separately.

Three tested interventions failed to validate a color correction. The C1 chroma-anchor candidate passed its four-object numeric gate (mean unseen-view $\Delta$FG-CIEDE2000 $=-1.5602$, 95\% CI $[-2.2621,-0.6299]$) but failed locked visual review, including a cyan/blue rim. B2's four-object numeric result was $+0.1729$ (95\% CI $[-0.2044,+0.6810]$), with only one of four objects improving and no clear visual correction. A feature-relative residual gate increased mean CIEDE2000 versus C3 by 1.35 across 26 objects and by 3.18 among the six earlier cases, with no clear visual reduction in the pink shift. These are sensitivity and failed-candidate results; no color-cast repair is validated.

The historical $N=20$ GLB-native check used 20 UV-compatible objects from the original 24-object pool and 11 unseen views, rendered with unlit base color. C3--GFL FG-PSNR was $-0.066$~dB (95\% CI $[-0.413,+0.290]$), FG-LPIPS was $-0.004719$ (95\% CI $[-0.007504,-0.002544]$), and CIEDE2000 was $+0.133$ (95\% CI $[-1.161,+1.319]$): endpoint directions are mixed, and these results do not establish full PBR/material fidelity or seam quality. The earlier Fresh C 24-object attempt failed its input gate and is retained as an implementation diagnostic. The five-object bake has now been rerun with corrected pole masks, scalar-alpha decoding and resolution-matched GT-256 inputs. Its descriptive C3--GFH PSNR difference is $+2.37$~dB, with lower SSIM; Late-high has higher mean PSNR and lower LPIPS than C3. This earlier pilot is not pooled with the new ten-object study in Section~\ref{subsec:new-bake}, and does not independently validate a universal C3 benefit. Separate REPEAT-addressed results also required a bilinear-weight correction. The historical $N=20$ study, this five-object archive, and the newly frozen technical cohort are not pooled. The stored GeoTex condition named native\_default\_1x is a Constant 1.0 request under native caps: its shallow correction is multiplied by 0.8, whereas the unset-scale wrapper applies the raw correction. A wrapper-forward check with a synthetic unit correction rejects equivalence of those scale paths; it is not a full generated-image comparison. This condition is therefore labeled Constant 1.0 (capped), not an unmodified pipeline.

Fresh B is a separate $N=150$ cohort and reports LLH against LFM-EXACT, not C3. The paired LLH--LFM-EXACT differences are $+0.325$~dB FG-PSNR (95\% CI $[+0.209,+0.446]$) and $-0.00460$ FG-LPIPS (95\% CI $[-0.00563,-0.00357]$); both intervals fall within the recorded practical margins of $\pm0.5$~dB and $\pm0.01$. The saved lock states a pre-run freeze time, but the earliest preserved commit containing it is later than that time. We therefore report Fresh B as retrospective sensitivity rather than authenticated preregistered confirmation.

A separate Core-7 summary uses the same 276 object labels and recorded checkpoint lineage as Fresh C but does not establish common runner or complete input-tensor identity across its seven conditions. Its post-hoc C3--GFH contrasts point in opposite directions for Full-view PSNR ($+0.725229$~dB, 95\% CI $[+0.647134,+0.806467]$) and FG-PSNR ($-1.214235$~dB, 95\% CI $[-1.313952,-1.114705]$). It remains a retrospective diagnostic, not a same-runner confirmation or reproduction of the original $+0.96$~dB result (Supplementary Section~S5).

The earlier A3b common-support calculation compared 10-step integrated raw $L_2$ norms across three layer groups. The saved corrections have different spatial resolutions (24$\times$16, 48$\times$32, and 96$\times$64), and the traces omit channel counts, so absolute norms are dimension-dependent across groups. We withdraw the reported 0/2,250 overlap as a cross-layer dose-support conclusion. Together with the Fresh B lock chronology, A3b remains retrospective sensitivity evidence. Its map shows response heterogeneity under the tested interventions, but does not identify a dose-independent layer-by-window effect or an optimal schedule.

A separate retrospective analysis on the \texttt{FRESH\_CONFIRM\_300} cohort found nine of ten plus-one-corrected associations between LLH--GFL image-space deltas and ground-truth descriptors; the FG-LPIPS/coverage test had adjusted $p=0.0508$. FG-PSNR means ranged from $+4.140$~dB in the lowest Laplacian-variance quartile to $-0.087$ and $-0.029$~dB in the upper two quartiles. These are cohort-specific associations, not a causal complexity effect, a threshold, a schedule selector, or a texture-fidelity result.
